sources.facts: Yale University Art Gallery excavation record: originally a dwelling with broadly unchanged exterior, with assembly and a baptistery with painted plaster found in 1932.

Angelo and Silver, 2024, report a merged nearly full-length south assembly Room 4, west-wall font of Room 6, a 3.60 m baptistery ceiling, a 1.75 m upper attic, approximate 0.37 m timber–earth roof, court benches and paving, low inward-shuttered windows in Rooms 4 and 5, high western assembly windows, and enclosed court-access roof stair 7A.
Anne Chen’s published geographic record cites Jennifer Baird, Ben Gourley, Simon James and Dan Stewart’s 2008 survey and identifies the religious phase of this trapezoidal excavated structure.
